title: Kingdom of Pinya
capsule: The Kingdom of Pinya was established on 7 February 1313 by Thihathu, a grandson of Kyaswa of the Pagan Empire, after the Myinsaing triumvirate dissolved, with Pinya becoming the de jure Pagan successor state controlling the central Irrawaddy plain and its two major rice-producing regions. The kingdom's cohesion was perpetually undermined by dynastic rivalry between the Pinya and Sagaing branches of the royal family: Sagaing formally separated as an independent kingdom in 1325, leaving Pinya weakened. Maw Shan raids devastated the central Irrawaddy valley in 1358–59 and 1362–63; in 1364 Maw forces sacked both Pinya and Sagaing, and the Ava kingdom was founded on 26 February 1365 by Thado Minbya, who unified the remnants of both kingdoms. Pinya's brief existence marks the fragmented interregnum between Pagan's collapse and the Ava consolidation.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's existence and approximate political extent are attested in Burmese chronicles, but precise boundary demarcations are not available; the polygon reflects scholarly estimates of the central Irrawaddy basin territory under Pinya sovereignty.
